subject: Secure SDLC evidence: canary deploy logs, signed commits, and secret handback

Cc: FinSight SOC2 Team <soc2@soc2.finsight.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Request: evidence for canary deployments, commit provenance, and secret handback

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SOC 2 intake for FinSight Bank we need a focused packet showing how Redwood handles the secure SDLC for production-facing changes. Specifically we need:
- A short manifest of signed commits (authors + commit SHAs + GPG signatures) for the last two canary releases (just metadata is fine).
- CI job output showing PR gating and that secrets are masked in logs (screenshot acceptable).
- The canonical escape/handback process for ephemeral CI credentials when a runner is decommissioned (steps and who signs off).
- The canary-deploy log showing rollout phases and automated rollback triggers for one recent deploy.

Deliverables can be redacted but must prove controls are in place. Target date: 2027-12-17 COB. If you want, we can accept a staged delivery (manifest + logs first).

Quick clarifying questions: is there a single runbook link we should reference, and who will be the internal point of contact for any follow-up?

Best,
Alice
Alice Turner
Senior Assessor, Orion Audit Group

--

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We'll produce a redacted packet that demonstrates provenance without exposing secrets. Plan:
1) Deliver commit manifest (CSV) for the two canary releases you referenced. The CSV will include commit SHA, author, PR number, signature present (yes/no), and short note about backporting.
2) Provide a canary-deploy log (anonymized timestamps and instance IDs) and the rollout threshold that triggered the automated rollback.
3) Screenshot of the CI job showing masked variables and PR gating.
4) Short runbook excerpt outlining ephemeral credential handback + signature steps.

Jonas will pull the commit/CI artifacts. Karthik will prod the runbook and add the credential handback snippet. I'll assemble and deliver as a single zip by 2027-12-16 afternoon (we can accelerate if you prefer).

One question: for the screenshot, do you need the full job trace or just the masked-variables view?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Adding the runbook excerpt for ephemeral credential handback. Short version:
1) Runner / ephemeral vault credential owner triggers 'handback' via internal API.
2) CI Manager verifies the credential has no active sessions and requests authorization from Deploy Authority (team leads + infra owner).
3) Authorization recorded in our change ledger with a unique transaction id; credentials are rotated via KMS and old tokens are revoked.
4) Keystore rotation and handback require two approvers when the change window is outside standard operating hours.

Proof artifacts included: change_ledger_txid=CL-20271215-9921 referenced in commit-manifest.csv; you can cross reference that entry with the deploy log.

Runbook link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/ephemeral-secret-handback (internal, access-controlled).

Marissa — can you attach the screenshot of the CI job that shows masked variables? That will satisfy the masked-log requirement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, CI/CD Controls
